# Terrain Scatter

Give any terrain your own trees, reeds or rocks, drawn on its squares the way the game draws Forest's trees: scattered over the square, swaying in the wind, with their own snow and cold versions. Name the pictures in a sprite pack, then scatter the pack on a terrain with `terrainscatter` lines in its `selectterr` block. [Limits](limits.md#terrain-scatter).

- **Pictures:** a .tga or .png in your mod's folder, named as `"./<file>"`, with transparency as in a `spr` picture. Paint the piece standing centred on the bottom row, with clear sides. CoE5SE cuts the clear edges and fits each picture to 64 x 64, or to 128 x 128 when a side is over 64, scaled down when it is bigger, never up.
- **Which lines draw:** a terrain with lines draws only them, in place of the game's own pieces; its ground stays. When several mods have lines on one terrain, the mod latest in the load order draws it.

!!! info "More in the game's manual"
    Making a terrain with `selectterr` is in Illwinter's official modding manual, under ["Terrain Modding"](https://www.illwinter.com/coe5/coe5modding.pdf#page=30).

## The starter mod

Launch CoE5 once with the `--dumptrees` command-line option (in Steam: **Properties → Launch Options**). CoE5SE writes the game's Forest and Dead Forest trees from `tree.trs` as a mod, `TreeStarter`, in `coe5se_trees` in the game's user folder: a folder of pictures for each version, a sheet `trees.tga` of every tree with its number, and a `.c5m` whose lines draw Forest, Enchanted Forest and Dead Forest with the game's own numbers. Copy its folder into your mods directory, enable it, and paint over its pictures. A later launch with `--dumptrees` writes only the files that aren't there.

### newspritepack "&lt;name&gt;" <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #newspritepack .command data-toc-label="newspritepack" data-added="3.10" }

Starts a sprite pack: the pictures named by the `spr "./<file>"` lines right under it, one file or folder a line. A folder ends in `/` and gives every .tga and .png in it. The pack ends at the first line with another command. Declare it above the `terrainscatter` and `terraincenter` lines that use it.

- **name:** The pack's name, in double quotes. One pack per name in a mod.

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    #!@newspritepack "Mallorn"
    #!@spr "./forest/"
    ```

    Or one picture a line:

    ```c5m
    #!@newspritepack "Old Man Willow"
    #!@spr "./dead/tree.tga"
    ```

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    newspritepack "Mallorn"
    spr "./forest/"
    ```

    Or one picture a line:

    ```c5se
    newspritepack "Old Man Willow"
    spr "./dead/tree.tga"
    ```

### terrainscatter "&lt;pack&gt;" &lt;count&gt; &lt;size&gt; &lt;sway&gt; &lt;shade&gt; [clearcenter &lt;radius&gt;] [version] <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #terrainscatter .command data-toc-label="terrainscatter" data-added="3.10" }

Scatters the pack's pictures over each square of the terrain selected with `selectterr`, each piece one of the pack's pictures. Forest's trees are `40 50 100 50`.

- **pack:** A sprite pack of your mod, by name in double quotes.
- **count:** Pieces on each square, 1 to 100, at full graphics detail. A version may give 0, so the piece isn't drawn on those squares.
- **size:** The pieces' height, 1 to 200 percent of a square.
- **sway:** How far the pieces sway, 0 (still) to 500 percent of Forest's trees.
- **shade:** 0 to 100: how much darker a piece may be drawn than its picture. 0 draws every piece as bright as its picture.
- **clearcenter radius:** Keeps the pieces out of a circle in the middle of the square, as the Brigand Lair's trees stand around it. The radius is 0 to 100 percent of a square.
- **version:** `snow` (snow ground: below temperature 1, so most Forest on Elysium in Winter), `cold` (a cold square) or `snowcold` (snow ground on a cold square). Makes the line a version of the nearest line above it with no version, drawn in its place on those squares. Snow ground on a cold square draws the `snowcold` version, else the `cold` one, else the `snow` one.

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    #!@terrainscatter "Mallorn" 30 60 100 50
    ```

    Or its version on a cold square:

    ```c5m
    #!@terrainscatter "Fir" 30 75 100 50 cold
    ```

    Or around a clear middle:

    ```c5m
    #!@terrainscatter "Mallorn" 15 75 100 50 clearcenter 40
    ```

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    terrainscatter "Mallorn" 30 60 100 50
    ```

    Or its version on a cold square:

    ```c5se
    terrainscatter "Fir" 30 75 100 50 cold
    ```

    Or around a clear middle:

    ```c5se
    terrainscatter "Mallorn" 15 75 100 50 clearcenter 40
    ```

### terraincenter "&lt;pack&gt;" &lt;size&gt; [version] <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #terraincenter .command data-toc-label="terraincenter" data-added="3.10" }

Draws one piece of the pack standing in the middle of each square of the terrain, still, as the game draws its towers.

- **pack:** A sprite pack of your mod, by name in double quotes.
- **size:** The piece's height, 1 to 200 percent of a square.
- **version:** `snow`, `cold` or `snowcold`, as for `terrainscatter`.

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    #!@terraincenter "Old Man Willow" 120
    ```

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    terraincenter "Old Man Willow" 120
    ```

## Terrain pictures

To check how your terrain looks without starting a game, launch CoE5 with `--dumpterrain <terrain> ...` (one or more terrain numbers or names, quoting a name with spaces). At the main menu, CoE5SE opens the map editor once, lays an 8 x 8 patch of each terrain in all four states (Plain, Cold, Snow, and Snow and cold), saves `<number>_<name>.tga` in `coe5se_terrain` in the game's user folder, and returns to the main menu.

## Forest rules

Vanilla ties three forest mechanics directly to Forest's terrain number (2), so adding `forest` to a mod's terrain does not give them to it. These four commands, used inside a `selectterr` block, add those rules to any terrain, forest or not. They don't change which terrains rituals target, though `fullforest`'s `forest` flag counts as `forest` does.

CoE5SE also applies a terrain's vanilla `destroyto` when a square is chopped (Chop & Burn), drained of lifeforce, or withered in Hades, as the game already does when it burns or is ruined.

### heartclaim <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #heartclaim .command data-toc-label="heartclaim" data-added="3.10" }

Lets the Heart of the Forest claim squares of this terrain the way it claims Forest.

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    selectterr 8
    #!@heartclaim
    ```

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    selectterr 8
    heartclaim
    ```

### wildspawn <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #wildspawn .command data-toc-label="wildspawn" data-added="3.10" }

Lets Call of the Wild spawn its animals on squares of this terrain the way it does on Forest and Ancient Forest.

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    selectterr 8
    #!@wildspawn
    ```

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    selectterr 8
    wildspawn
    ```

### hotconvert &lt;terrain nbr&gt; <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #hotconvert .command data-toc-label="hotconvert" data-added="3.10" }

Turns squares of this terrain into the given terrain when their temperature is above 65 (above 100, the game's own change to Desert runs instead), at (temperature - 65)% a month, as heat turns Forest into Savanna. On Plain, this runs before Plain's own change to Savanna or Desert. When several mods give a terrain `hotconvert`, the mod latest in the load order decides.

- **terrain nbr:** The terrain number heat turns the square into, as `destroyto` takes.

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    selectterr 593
    #!@hotconvert 36
    ```

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    selectterr 593
    hotconvert 36
    ```

### fullforest <span class="new-badge">New</span> { #fullforest .command data-toc-label="fullforest" data-added="3.10" }

Gives this terrain the `forest` flag, `heartclaim`, `wildspawn`, and `hotconvert 119` (Savanna). A `hotconvert` line after it sets a different terrain for heat to turn it into. Write `forest` in your `.c5m` and `#!@ fullforest` after it if you want the mod to load as a plain forest without CoE5SE.

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    selectterr 593
    forest
    #!@fullforest
    ```

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    selectterr 593
    forest
    fullforest
    ```

### Example terrain scatter and forest rules { #example }

Mallorn trees on every Forest, firs on its cold squares, both under snow in Winter, Old Man Willow in the middle of each Ancient Forest, `heartclaim` and `wildspawn` on Enchanted Forest, and `fullforest` with `hotconvert` to Dead Forest on Fangorn:

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    #!@newspritepack "Mallorn"
    #!@spr "./forest/"
    #!@newspritepack "Mallorn in Winter"
    #!@spr "./snow/"
    #!@newspritepack "Fir"
    #!@spr "./cold/"
    #!@newspritepack "Fir in Winter"
    #!@spr "./snowcold/"
    #!@newspritepack "Old Man Willow"
    #!@spr "./dead/tree.tga"

    selectterr 2
    #!@terrainscatter "Mallorn" 30 60 100 50
    #!@terrainscatter "Mallorn in Winter" 30 60 100 50 snow
    #!@terrainscatter "Fir" 30 75 100 50 cold
    #!@terrainscatter "Fir in Winter" 30 75 100 50 snowcold

    selectterr 4
    #!@terraincenter "Old Man Willow" 120
    #!@terrainscatter "Mallorn" 15 75 100 50 clearcenter 40

    selectterr 8
    #!@heartclaim
    #!@wildspawn

    selectterr 593
    #!@fullforest
    #!@hotconvert 36
    ```

=== ".c5se"

    ```c5se
    newspritepack "Mallorn"
    spr "./forest/"
    newspritepack "Mallorn in Winter"
    spr "./snow/"
    newspritepack "Fir"
    spr "./cold/"
    newspritepack "Fir in Winter"
    spr "./snowcold/"
    newspritepack "Old Man Willow"
    spr "./dead/tree.tga"

    selectterr 2
    terrainscatter "Mallorn" 30 60 100 50
    terrainscatter "Mallorn in Winter" 30 60 100 50 snow
    terrainscatter "Fir" 30 75 100 50 cold
    terrainscatter "Fir in Winter" 30 75 100 50 snowcold

    selectterr 4
    terraincenter "Old Man Willow" 120
    terrainscatter "Mallorn" 15 75 100 50 clearcenter 40

    selectterr 8
    heartclaim
    wildspawn

    selectterr 593
    fullforest
    hotconvert 36
    ```
